# Introduction

This report takes the imported dataset from report 1, puts its timepoints on the right clock,
and runs the time-course processing steps: `create_SE()` and `normalize_SE()`.

The clock matters more than it sounds. Everything downstream — log fold change, growth rates,
the dose-response fits in report 3 — is anchored on time zero, and in this dataset time zero is
not where the instrument put it.

```{r libraries}
library(qs2)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
library(gDRutils)
library(gDRcore)
library(gDRplots)


```

```{r get_wd}
wd <- getwd()
for (d in c("plots", "gDR_data", "tables")) {
  dir.create(file.path(wd, d), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
}
data_imported <- qs_read(file.path(wd, "gDR_data", "gDR_input.qs2"))


```

# The instrument clock is not the experiment clock

The `Elapsed` column of an Incucyte export counts from the moment imaging starts, which here is
**plating**. Treatment starts later, and not at the same time on every plate — the published
plate table says so:

```{r t0_table}
plate_tab <- fread("raw_data/20160421_MCF10A LINCS_drug response live_plateID.tsv")
generate_datatable(plate_tab[, .(Barcode, Tplate_Date, T0date, plating_delay)])


```

All six plates were seeded on 2016-04-20 at 1 pm. Plates X01-X03 were treated 24 h later and
plates X04-X06 48 h later, so `Duration == 0` means "one day before treatment" on half the
plates and "two days before" on the other half. Left alone, any time window mixes
pre-treatment growth with post-treatment response, and the two plate groups contribute
different amounts of each.

```{r raw_growth_plot, fig.height=5, fig.width=10}
vehicle_traces <- data_imported[Gnumber == "vehicle",
                                .(count = mean(ReadoutValue)),
                                by = .(Barcode, Duration)]

p_raw <- ggplot(vehicle_traces, aes(Duration, count, colour = Barcode)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(24, 48), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  annotate("text", x = 24, y = Inf, label = "T0 for X01-X03", hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.5, size = 3) +
  annotate("text", x = 48, y = Inf, label = "T0 for X04-X06", hjust = -0.05, vjust = 3.0, size = 3) +
  labs(title = "Vehicle wells on the instrument clock",
       subtitle = "Mean cell count per plate; dashed lines mark the two treatment starts",
       x = "Elapsed since plating (h)", y = "Mean cell count") +
  theme_bw()

ggsave(file.path(wd, "plots", "qc_vehicle_raw_clock.svg"), p_raw,
       width = 10, height = 5, device = "svg")
p_raw


```

## Snapping to the nearest image, not to the nominal hour

Subtracting a nominal 24 h or 48 h is not enough. Imaging runs on its own grid and does not
land on the treatment hour, so a plain subtraction leaves the earliest timepoint at 0.08 h
rather than 0. `normalize_SE_time_course()` anchors on an exact `Duration == 0` row; without
one it warns, returns the object unnormalized, and the run fails several steps later in
`fit_SE.timecourse()` with a message about a missing `LogFoldChange` assay.

The fix is to subtract the observed timepoint closest to T0, so that image becomes time zero.

```{r shift_clock}
dt <- copy(data_imported)
dt[, nominal_t0 := fifelse(grepl("_X0[123]$", Barcode), 24, 48)]
dt[, observed_t0 := Duration[which.min(abs(Duration - nominal_t0))], by = Barcode]

generate_datatable(
  unique(dt[, .(Barcode, nominal_t0, observed_t0,
                offset = round(observed_t0 - nominal_t0, 3))])
)

dt[, Duration := round(Duration - observed_t0, 4)]
dt <- dt[Duration >= 0]
dt[, c("nominal_t0", "observed_t0") := NULL]

stopifnot(any(dt$Duration == 0))


```

Timepoints before treatment are dropped: they describe untreated cells and have no place in a
dose-response. This is a property of the experiment, not of gDR, which is why it lives in the
report rather than in the pipeline.

```{r shifted_summary}
data.table(
  Metric = c("rows before shift", "rows after shift", "timepoints kept",
             "duration range (h)"),
  Value = c(format(nrow(data_imported), big.mark = " "),
            format(nrow(dt), big.mark = " "),
            uniqueN(dt$Duration),
            paste(range(dt$Duration), collapse = " - "))
) |> generate_datatable()


```

# Processing

With the clock fixed, gDR recognises the data as time-course on its own: multiple records share
the same barcode and well, which is what `data_model()` keys on.

```{r data_model}
data_model(dt)


```

```{r create_se}
se <- create_SE(dt, data_type = "time-course")
se


```

```{r normalize_se}
se <- normalize_SE(se, data_type = "time-course")
SummarizedExperiment::assayNames(se)


```

`normalize_SE()` adds the `LogFoldChange` assay: for every well, the log2 ratio of its count at
each timepoint to its own count at time zero. Normalizing each well against itself, rather than
against a plate control, is what makes the trajectories comparable across plates seeded at
slightly different densities.

# Quality control

```{r lfc_controls, fig.height=5, fig.width=10}
lfc <- convert_se_assay_to_dt(se, "LogFoldChange")

ctrl <- lfc[Gnumber == "vehicle", .(lfc = mean(LogFoldChange, na.rm = TRUE)),
            by = .(Barcode, Duration)]

p_ctrl <- ggplot(ctrl, aes(Duration, lfc, colour = Barcode)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "Untreated growth after anchoring on treatment start",
       subtitle = "Mean log2 fold change of vehicle wells; a straight line means exponential growth",
       x = "Time since treatment (h)", y = "log2 fold change") +
  theme_bw()

ggsave(file.path(wd, "plots", "qc_vehicle_lfc.svg"), p_ctrl,
       width = 10, height = 5, device = "svg")
p_ctrl


```

Vehicle wells should climb roughly linearly on this scale — MCF10A doubles about once a day —
and the six plates should agree. Divergence between plates here would point at a seeding or an
edge problem rather than at a drug effect.

```{r lfc_by_drug, fig.height=9, fig.width=11}
treated <- lfc[Gnumber != "vehicle"]
treated[, conc_band := cut(Concentration,
                           breaks = quantile(unique(Concentration), probs = seq(0, 1, 0.25)),
                           include.lowest = TRUE, labels = c("Q1 low", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4 high"))]

traces <- treated[, .(lfc = mean(LogFoldChange, na.rm = TRUE)),
                  by = .(DrugName, conc_band, Duration)]

p_drugs <- ggplot(traces, aes(Duration, lfc, colour = conc_band)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ DrugName, ncol = 3) +
  labs(title = "Response trajectories by drug and concentration band",
       subtitle = "Mean log2 fold change; flattening or falling curves indicate growth arrest or cell loss",
       x = "Time since treatment (h)", y = "log2 fold change", colour = "Concentration") +
  theme_bw()

ggsave(file.path(wd, "plots", "qc_lfc_by_drug.svg"), p_drugs,
       width = 11, height = 9, device = "svg")
p_drugs


```

Reading this panel is the quickest check that the import is sound. A cytotoxic agent at its top
concentrations should bend away from the vehicle curve within a day; an agent that only slows
the cells should stay positive but shallower. A drug whose bands are indistinguishable either
has no effect in this cell line or was mapped to the wrong wells.

```{r save_se}
qs_save(se, file.path(wd, "gDR_data", "gDR_se_normalized.qs2"))


```

# Conclusion

The timepoints are anchored on treatment start, the data are recognised as time-course, and the
normalized `SummarizedExperiment` is saved to `gDR_data/gDR_se_normalized.qs2`. Report 3 turns
the trajectories into growth rates and fits dose-response curves to them.
